$schema-note: Per-store listing field limits (FR-109, contract L1). These are facts about two products owned by other companies, not about this project: they change without notice and silently truncate rather than erroring. Recorded here once so the gate reads them as data and a store's layout change is a data edit. Counted in Unicode code points.

assets.$note: What each committed artefact must be for its store to accept it (FR-111, contract L8). Dimensions and alpha are read from the PNG header by the gate — no image dependency (Principle II). Three of these are rejection-at-review conditions rather than cosmetic ones, and each is marked.

listing/assets/icon-ios-1024.png.note: REJECTION CONDITION. Apple rejects an app icon with an alpha channel and one with pre-applied corner rounding. An icon exported from a design tool with a transparent background looks correct everywhere except at submission.

listing/assets/icon-adaptive-foreground..note: The launcher masks this to a shape the device chooses, so every meaningful pixel sits inside the centre safe zone. Transparency is the point here — an opaque foreground defeats the mask.

listing/assets/feature-graphic-1024x500..note: REJECTION CONDITION. Play will not publish a listing without a feature graphic, and it is the asset most easily forgotten because no other store has an equivalent.

ios.requiredBy: App Store — a 6.9" iPhone set; the store derives the smaller sizes from it

android.requiredBy: Google Play — 2 to 8 phone screenshots in total
android.note: REJECTION CONDITION. Play requires the longest side to be no more than twice the shortest. A modern phone emulator boots at 1080×2400, which is 2.22:1 and is rejected — so the capture profile is pinned to 1080×1920 (1.78:1) and the gate checks the committed pixels rather than trusting the device profile.
